castanas.title: Air fryer roasted chestnuts: how to score and peel them
castanas.summary: Roast fresh chestnuts in the air fryer with a short soak and a damp-cloth rest. An autumn snack with a tender centre, ready to peel while warm.
steps: Sort and wash
Choose firm edible chestnuts without holes or mould. Wash and discard damaged ones. Use culinary chestnuts, never horse chestnuts.
Score every chestnut
Place each chestnut flat-side down on a stable board. Carefully cut a horizontal slit through the shell and inner skin without cutting deeply into the flesh. Score every chestnut before heating.
Soak
Cover the scored chestnuts with the water and soak for 20 minutes. Drain well; the soak helps soften the shell but does not replace scoring.
Prepare the basket
Preheat the air fryer to 180 °C for 3 minutes. Arrange the drained chestnuts in one layer, slits facing upwards. Cook in batches if necessary.
Start roasting
Roast at 180 °C for 10 minutes. Shake the basket carefully to redistribute them; the slits should start to open.
Check the centre
Roast for another 5–8 minutes. Open one carefully: the centre must be tender. If still firm, continue in 2-minute intervals; size and appliance affect the timing.
Rest and peel warm
Wrap in a clean damp cloth for 5 minutes. Peel the shell and inner skin while still warm, working in small batches and protecting your fingers from the heat.
Serve
Divide between four portions and serve warm. Discard any chestnut with an unusual smell or colour inside. Additional air-fryer batches extend the total time.
castanas.notes: The 500 g includes shells; nutrition estimates 350 g edible chestnuts, divided into four portions. This yield varies. Never heat unscored chestnuts. Refrigerate peeled leftovers within 2 hours and use within 2 days. Reheat briefly covered so they do not dry out.
faq: Why score chestnuts before cooking?
The opening lets steam escape and makes peeling easier. Pierce both the shell and inner skin of every chestnut.
Can I roast them without soaking?
Yes, but the shell can be harder to remove. This recipe includes a 20-minute soak; it does not guarantee every variety will peel equally easily.
How do I know they are done?
Taste a carefully opened chestnut: its centre should be tender, without a firm raw core. Open shells alone are not proof of doneness.

garbanzos.title: Marry Me Chickpeas with sun-dried tomatoes and spinach
garbanzos.summary: Canned chickpeas simmered in a creamy sun-dried tomato, spinach and Parmesan sauce. This one-pan Marry Me Chickpeas recipe makes four comforting portions.
steps: Prepare the ingredients
Drain and rinse the chickpeas to obtain 480 g. Chop the onion and garlic, slice the drained tomatoes into strips and wash the spinach.
Soften the onion
Heat 15 g oil in a wide skillet over medium heat. Add the onion and cook, stirring, for 6–7 minutes until softened without burning.
Build the sauce base
Add the garlic, sun-dried tomatoes, 20 g tomato paste and oregano. Stir for 2 minutes to cook the tomato paste.
Add the chickpeas
Pour in 200 ml broth and scrape the bottom with a spoon. Add the chickpeas and simmer gently, uncovered, for 5 minutes.
Stir in the cream
Lower the heat and add 150 g cream. Simmer very gently for 6–8 minutes, until the sauce coats the chickpeas without drying out.
Wilt the spinach
Add the spinach in two batches and stir for 2 minutes until wilted and evenly distributed. Avoid unnecessary prolonged boiling.
Finish off the heat
Turn off the heat and stir in the Parmesan and pepper. Taste before adding the 2 g salt: the broth and cheese may already provide enough.
Serve
Divide between four plates and serve hot. Bread or rice served alongside is not included in the ingredient quantities or nutrition.
garbanzos.notes: Use already cooked chickpeas; dried ones need a separate cooking process. Traditional Parmesan may use animal rennet: choose cheese made with microbial rennet for a strict vegetarian version. Contains milk. Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and use within 3 days; reheat gently with a little water. Nutrition includes all the listed salt, even if you use less.
faq: What are Marry Me Chickpeas?
Chickpeas in a creamy sun-dried tomato sauce inspired by Marry Me Chicken. This recipe contains no chicken.
Can I replace the cream with milk?
Not in the same quantity for this texture. Milk has less fat and thickens differently; this formulation is calculated for heavy cream.
Can I freeze it?
Yes, although the sauce may separate. Thaw in the refrigerator and reheat gently while stirring; the texture is best freshly made.

zwiebel.title: Zwiebelkuchen: German onion cake with yeast dough
zwiebel.summary: A savoury German onion tart with a soft yeast base, slowly softened onions, bacon, sour cream and caraway. Make one 28 cm tart to cut into eight portions.
steps: Knead the dough
Mix flour, lukewarm milk, yeast, sugar, softened butter and 4 g salt. Knead for 8–10 minutes until smooth; the milk must not be hot.
Let it rise
Cover the dough in a bowl and leave in a warm, draught-free place for about 60 minutes, until roughly doubled in volume.
Prepare the filling
Thinly slice the 900 g peeled onions and dice the bacon. Weigh the sour cream and 100 g egg without shells; keep them chilled until mixing.
Cook and cool the onions
Cook the bacon in a wide pan for 5 minutes. Add the onions and cook gently for 15 minutes, stirring until soft. Take off the heat and cool for 10 minutes.
Line the tin
Roll out the dough and line a 28 cm springform tin, making a 3 cm rim. Rest for 15 minutes while preheating the oven to 180 °C, conventional heat.
Mix the filling
Whisk eggs, sour cream, caraway, pepper and the remaining 2 g salt. Fold in the cooled onion and bacon mixture and spread over the dough.
Bake
Bake at 180 °C for 40–45 minutes until the base is cooked and the centre is set. Cover the rim if browning too quickly; extend cooking if the filling is still liquid.
Rest and slice
Rest in the tin for 10 minutes, then carefully release the sides and cut into eight portions. Serve warm with a simple salad if desired.
zwiebel.notes: Use baker’s yeast, not baking powder, and caraway, not cumin. Contains wheat, milk and eggs. The stated total allows for rising, filling cooling, the second dough rest and resting after baking; some tasks overlap. Refrigerate within 2 hours and use within 3 days. Nutrition counts the rendered bacon fat retained in the filling; any accompanying salad is excluded.
faq: Can I make Zwiebelkuchen ahead?
Yes. Refrigerate the baked tart and reheat portions in the oven until hot throughout. The base is best on the first day.
Why cook the onions first?
It softens them, removes some water and prevents a wet filling with raw onion inside.
Can I omit the bacon?
Yes, but use a little additional fat to soften the onions. That variation changes the flavour and the calculated nutrition.

lentejas.title: Warm lentil and roasted carrot salad with Dijon dressing
lentejas.summary: Green lentils, roasted carrots and toasted walnuts tossed with a mustard and cider-vinegar dressing. A French-inspired salad for four, served warm or chilled.
steps: Prepare the carrots
Heat the oven to 200 °C, conventional heat. Cut the carrots into 1 cm half-moons. Rinse the lentils and remove any stones or damaged seeds.
Roast
Toss the carrots with 15 g oil and 2 g salt. Spread on a tray and roast for 25–30 minutes, turning halfway, until tender and lightly browned.
Cook the lentils
Meanwhile, cover the lentils with 1 litre water in a saucepan. Simmer gently for 20–30 minutes, until tender but holding their shape; add water if needed.
Make the dressing
Finely chop the shallot. Whisk the Dijon mustard, vinegar, remaining 20 g oil, remaining 2 g salt and pepper, then add the shallot.
Drain well
Drain the cooked lentils in a sieve for 2 minutes. Avoid rinsing if serving warm; excess water would dilute the dressing.
Toast the walnuts
Roughly chop the walnuts and toast in a dry pan for 2–3 minutes, stirring and watching closely so they do not burn. Chop the parsley.
Combine
Toss the warm lentils with the dressing, roasted carrots, walnuts and parsley. Fold gently to keep the lentils intact.
Serve
Divide into four portions and serve warm, or cool promptly and refrigerate for a cold salad. Bread and additional toppings are excluded from the nutrition.
lentejas.notes: Contains walnuts and mustard. Refrigerate within 2 hours and use within 3 days. You may substitute 600 g cooked, drained lentils, but the timing and nutrition will differ from this dry-lentil formulation. All the listed salt is included in the estimate. Use green lentils that hold their shape rather than split red lentils.
faq: Can I use canned lentils?
Yes, use about 600 g after draining. Warm them gently and skip boiling; the published nutrition is based on 250 g dried lentils.
Can I serve it cold?
Yes. Cool promptly, refrigerate and stir before serving, as the lentils absorb dressing.
How can I replace the walnuts?
For a nut-free version, omit them and check other ingredients for cross-contact. This changes the texture and nutrition.

chocolate.title: Thick Italian hot chocolate with dark chocolate
chocolate.summary: Italian-style hot chocolate with milk, cocoa and dark chocolate, thickened with a little cornstarch. Four small cups with a rich, spoonable texture.
steps: Chop the chocolate
Finely chop the dark chocolate so it melts evenly. Measure the milk and set aside 100 ml cold; keep the remaining 400 ml separate.
Mix the dry ingredients
Sift cocoa and cornstarch into a bowl. Add the sugar and mix, breaking up any lumps before adding liquid.
Make a smooth slurry
Whisk the reserved 100 ml cold milk into the dry ingredients a little at a time until smooth, with no dry pockets.
Warm the milk
Heat the remaining 400 ml milk in a saucepan over medium-low heat until steaming. Do not let it boil over.
Thicken
Whisk in the cocoa mixture. Cook at a gentle bubble for 2–3 minutes, stirring constantly along the bottom, until the mixture coats a spoon.
Melt the chocolate
Remove from the heat and add the chopped chocolate. Stir until completely melted and glossy; avoid hard boiling after adding it.
Pour
Divide between four heatproof cups, about 150 ml each. The chocolate should fall from the spoon in a thick ribbon; it thickens further as it cools.
Serve carefully
Let stand briefly so it is comfortable to drink or eat with a spoon. Serve without extra cream or toppings to match the listed ingredients and nutrition.
chocolate.notes: Contains milk. Cornstarch means corn starch, not cornmeal. These are four small, rich cups, not large mugs. Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and use within 2 days. Reheat gently, stirring; extra milk changes the quantities and nutrition. The estimate uses a generic 70–85% dark chocolate reference, so your brand may differ.
faq: Why is Italian hot chocolate so thick?
This version combines dark chocolate with a small amount of cornstarch cooked in milk. It is intended to be spoonable.
Can I leave out the cornstarch?
You can, but it will be thinner and no longer match this formulation. Do not replace it with wheat flour in the same amount.
Why are there lumps?
Starch must first be mixed with cold milk. Sifting the powders and whisking continuously during cooking also helps.

daigaku.title: Daigaku imo: candied Japanese sweet potatoes in a pan
daigaku.summary: Purple-skinned Japanese sweet potatoes with a glossy sugar-and-soy glaze and black sesame. This microwave-and-pan version uses less oil than deep frying.
steps: Cut the sweet potato
Scrub the sweet potatoes and remove damaged areas. Cut into irregular pieces about 3 cm across, retaining the purple skin.
Soak and dry
Soak in water for 5 minutes, then drain and dry thoroughly with a clean cloth. Surface water causes splattering in hot oil.
Microwave
Place in a microwave-safe dish, cover with a vented lid and cook at 600 W for about 5 minutes. Check with a skewer; continue in 30-second intervals until just tender.
Brown in the pan
Heat 25 g oil in a wide pan over medium heat. Add the dried, precooked pieces and cook for 8–10 minutes, turning gently until several sides are golden.
Prepare the glaze
In a separate clean pan, heat the sugar, 30 ml water and soy sauce. Simmer for 1–2 minutes until large glossy bubbles form; do not reduce to a dark, hard caramel.
Coat
Add the warm sweet potatoes to the glaze and toss gently over low heat for about 30 seconds, until glossy and coated. Keep pieces intact.
Add sesame and cool
Sprinkle with black sesame and spread on baking parchment, separating the pieces. Cool for 5 minutes; the sugar glaze is extremely hot straight from the pan.
Serve
Divide into four portions and serve once the glaze is safe to eat. The coating is best freshly made; avoid touching or tasting hot syrup.
daigaku.notes: Contains soy, sesame and usually wheat from soy sauce. This version uses microwave cooking and pan browning, rather than traditional double deep frying. Nutrition conservatively counts all 25 g oil. Purple-skinned, yellow-fleshed Japanese sweet potatoes hold their shape well; orange varieties are more fragile. Best eaten fresh; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and use within 1 day, accepting a softer glaze.
faq: Can I use orange sweet potatoes?
Yes, but they are softer and may break when coated. Check microwave doneness earlier and turn gently.
Why is the coating hard?
The syrup may have reduced too far. Stop at large bubbles and a glossy coating; do not cook it to a dark caramel.
Can I make it without a microwave?
Steam the pieces until just tender, then let the surface dry thoroughly before pan browning. Cooking and total times will change.

farofa.title: Plantain farofa with toasted cassava flour
farofa.summary: Brazilian farofa with ripe cooking plantain, butter and toasted cassava meal. A loose, golden side dish for six, ready in about 30 minutes.
steps: Cut the plantain
Peel the ripe cooking plantain and weigh 300 g flesh. Cut into 1.5 cm cubes; choose ripe but firm fruit that will hold its shape.
Prepare the aromatics
Finely chop the onion and chives. Weigh 180 g toasted cassava meal and divide the butter into 20 g and 15 g portions.
Brown the plantain
Melt 20 g butter in a wide pan over medium heat. Cook the plantain for 5–7 minutes, turning carefully, until golden on several sides.
Set aside
Transfer the plantain to a plate without crushing it. Leave the browned butter in the pan, provided it has not burned.
Soften the onion
Add the remaining 15 g butter and the onion. Cook for 5–6 minutes, stirring, until softened and lightly golden.
Toast the meal
Add the toasted cassava meal and stir over medium-low heat for 3–4 minutes. It should smell toasted and stay loose, without becoming a paste.
Combine gently
Return the plantain, add chives, salt and pepper, and fold gently for 1 minute. Avoid crushing the fruit and do not add water.
Serve
Transfer to a serving dish and divide into six side portions. Serve warm alongside beans or a main dish; accompaniments are not included in the nutrition.
farofa.notes: Use coarse toasted cassava meal (farinha de mandioca torrada), not tapioca starch, and cooking plantain rather than a soft dessert banana. Contains milk from butter. Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and use within 2 days; reheat in a dry pan. Cassava-flour nutrition uses the Brazilian TBCA reference; total sugars are omitted because that reference does not provide a complete value.
faq: Is cassava meal the same as tapioca starch?
No. Farofa needs toasted, granular cassava meal. Fine tapioca starch makes a different texture and is not a direct substitute.
Can I use a dessert banana?
It is softer and sweeter and breaks more easily. This recipe and its nutrition use ripe cooking plantain.
Why is my farofa wet?
Very soft fruit or added liquid can make it clump. Keep the plantain firm, brown it separately and add no water.
